items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Then he signed Count Basie, then he signed Billie Holiday and on and on

ctx.x: No. That’s what I talk about in my class and that’s where integration — when John Hammond, who I’m sure you know, knew, or know of — well I was lucky enough to know John Hammond. He worked at two labels, Columbia and Vanguard. I worked at two labels, Columbia and Vanguard. And I got to know Mr. Hammond in the 80s. He died in ’87. But he was the guy who integrated the Goodman band in 1935 by getting him to hire Teddy Wilson and then Lionel Hampton and then Charlie Christian. And he told me stories that are just…

items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: he paid for the sessions for Basie and Billie Holiday

ctx.x: Yes. So he had the sort of financial luxury of taking these causes and really getting behind them.
As he said, “I had the means to pay for my” — he paid for the sessions for Basie and Billie Holiday. He paid for those things himself. He was his own bank for that stuff.

There’s some real gems on the thing and I was listening to the one, “Stompin’ at the Savoy” with the Benny Goodman Sextet. And I hadn’t looked at the personnel but I am hearing this chomp-chomp-chomp-chomp — and I go man, Freddie Green’s really going at it. And then I looked and it was Charlie Christian. And that surprised me I guess because I’m not sure I had heard Charlie Christian do that. I was more familiar with his soloing.
